title: My first time planning a Unity game project. Want to create a cozy travelling-inn RPG. I would like to hear your suggestions.
author: crazymicheosso
selftext:
I’m currently studying web development. Cuz I enjoyed planning games quite a lot, especially those allowing for slow exploration and management. Like farming, management, light RPGs, collection and cultivation games. I really get into these types.



I’ve been thinking about creating a truly playable small game by myself. Not that kind of quickly ends after two clicks demo. I want to create something with a sense of completion even if it’s on a smaller scale.



My current idea is to create a small-scale RPG. The core gameplay is roughly like:

* Go out to explore a small area, gather materials, collect ingredients and encounter NPCs.
* Back at the traveling-inn. The collected items were used for cooking, repainting furniture and decorating the room.
* Serving guests, arrange rooms according to their preferences and do some little requests.
* Gradually upgrade the hotel. unlock new rooms, new decoration and new areas.



I don’t want to create a kind of business simulation game that can make players feel stressed like doing calculations all the time. I’d like to make it feel like slowly rebuilding the run-down hotel. It’s a bit like when you first take over a rundown hotel and gradually transform into a warm little house. Guests come and go but some people keep showing up, gradually forming a connection with players.



I plan to keep the scope very limited rn. The first version might only cover one region, 3 - 4 types of guests, a few upgradeable rooms, a simple backpack system and a little bit of conversation content. I need to make this small loop work smoothly first, otherwise it will feel like too much to handle if I start with a large map, a big plot, and a complex system from the beginning.



The tools I was thinking rn is:

* Blender – used to create a low-poly furniture, rooms, props and scene assets. It’s also convenient for adjusting the models later.
* Unity – As the main engine. I know something about it so I don’t start from scratch completely at least.
* Tripo AI – Used to quickly generate some initial models such as props, furniture, and small buildings as rough prototypes or inspiration references. Then import them into Blender to clean, modify and unify the style.
* Substance Painter – It can be used to create stylized materials if more detailed textures are needed later.
* Quixel Bridge – Primarily used to find some temporary placeholders for scenes, facilitating the setup of the initial scene and testing the atmosphere.



Well this is basically my current idea. I’d love to hear your suggestions. Oh and also I’d love to know your opinion about cozy traveling-inn concepts.

comments.author: Harper_Phillipss
comments.body: Honestly this is a great scope for a solo Unity project. If you keep the guest interactions simple but meaningful, it could get really addictive in a Stardew-meets-inn vibe.
